title: Kaba Gandhi No Delo - The Ancestral Home of Mahatma Gandhi in Rajkot
content:
Kaba Gandhi No Delo,

Nestled in the heart of Rajkot city, Kaba Gandhi No Delo holds immense historical and emotional significance as it was the ancestral home of Mahatma Gandhi, the Father of the Nation. The name “Kaba Gandhi No Delo” translates to “Kaba Gandhi’s house”, referring to Karamchand Gandhi, Mahatma Gandhi’s father, who served as a Diwan (chief minister) of Rajkot.

This humble yet iconic house has been converted into a museum that beautifully preserves the memories and legacy of Mahatma Gandhi’s early life.

A Glimpse into Gandhi’s Early Life

Kaba Gandhi No Delo offers visitors an intimate look at Gandhi’s formative years, long before he became the global icon of peace and non-violence. The museum houses rare photographs, personal belongings, handwritten letters, and artifacts depicting various stages of his journey-from his childhood in Rajkot to his time in South Africa and his return to India to lead the freedom movement.

The interiors of the house reflect the traditional architecture of Saurashtra, with wooden balconies, open courtyards, and old-style rooms that exude a sense of simplicity—perfectly aligned with Gandhi’s philosophy of minimalism and truth.

Museum Highlights

  • Photo Gallery: A collection of old photographs depicting Gandhiji’s life and struggles.
  • Personal Artifacts: Items used by Gandhi and his family, giving visitors a sense of his modest lifestyle.
  • Library: A reading space that contains books on Gandhi’s philosophy, Indian history, and freedom movements.
  • Cultural Programs: Occasionally, events and talks on Gandhian values are organized to educate young minds.

Architectural Beauty

The architecture of Kaba Gandhi No Delo is a fine example of 19th-century Saurashtrian design, featuring carved wooden balconies, traditional windows, and an open courtyard that symbolizes harmony and simplicity. The peaceful ambiance instantly transports visitors back in time, offering a glimpse of the environment that shaped Gandhi’s thoughts and principles.

Location and Timings

Location: Gheekantha Road, Rajkot, Gujarat
Visiting Hours: 9:00 AM - 12:00 PM and 3:00 PM - 6:00 PM (Closed on Sundays)
Entry Fee: Free (donations accepted)

How to Reach

  • By Air: The nearest airport is Rajkot Airport, around 3 km away.
  • By Train: Rajkot Junction Railway Station is just 2 km from the site.
  • By Road: Easily accessible by auto-rickshaw or taxi from any part of the city.
